title: Directions and Distance Reasoning — Part 2 of 10

questions.question: What is a 'reference frame' in direction reasoning?
options: The fixed coordinate system or starting orientation against which all other directions and positions are measured
A physical picture frame
A synonym for distance
Only used in 3D problems
questions.rationale: A reference frame is the fixed coordinate system or starting orientation that all directions and positions in a problem are measured against.

questions.question: What does 'heading' refer to?
options: The title of a reasoning question
The total distance traveled so far
The current direction someone or something is facing or moving
A synonym for position
questions.rationale: Heading describes the current direction something is facing or moving in, which can change over the course of a multi-step problem.

questions.question: How many directions does the 'eight-direction heading' system include?
questions.rationale: The eight-direction system includes N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, and NW — the four cardinal directions plus the four intercardinal directions.

questions.question: What is a 'bearing'?
options: A type of distance unit
A fixed physical landmark
A synonym for displacement
A direction expressed as an angle, commonly measured clockwise from North
questions.rationale: A bearing expresses direction numerically as an angle, typically measured clockwise starting from North (0 degrees).

questions.question: What does 'position difference' measure between two points?
options: The change in coordinates (and therefore direction and distance) from one point to the other
Only the time between two events
The number of turns taken
The elevation difference only
questions.rationale: Position difference captures how coordinates change from one point to another, which is what lets you derive both the direction and distance between them.

questions.question: How can direction be determined from two coordinate points?
options: It cannot be determined from coordinates alone
By comparing their relative x and y differences to determine the angle/compass direction between them
By measuring the time it takes to travel between them
By counting the number of turns in between
questions.rationale: The relative difference in x and y coordinates between two points determines the angle (and therefore compass direction) from one to the other.

questions.question: What is 'Euclidean distance'?
options: The distance measured only along horizontal and vertical paths
The straight-line distance between two points, calculated using the Pythagorean-style formula
A distance measured in degrees
The total path length actually walked
questions.rationale: Euclidean distance is the straight-line ('as the crow flies') distance between two points, computed with the Pythagorean formula on their coordinate differences.

questions.question: What is 'Manhattan distance'?
options: The straight-line distance between two points
The distance between two points measured only along horizontal and vertical paths (sum of absolute coordinate differences), not diagonally
A distance measured only in miles
The distance around a full circular loop
questions.rationale: Manhattan distance sums the absolute horizontal and vertical differences between two points, modeling movement restricted to a grid rather than a direct diagonal line.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'path distance' and 'displacement'?
options: They always have the same value
Path distance is the total distance actually traveled along a route; displacement is the straight-line distance from start to end point
Displacement is always longer than path distance
Path distance only applies to circular routes
questions.rationale: Path distance totals every segment actually walked, while displacement is just the straight-line distance between the starting point and the final point, which is often shorter.

questions.question: If someone walks 3 km east then 4 km north, what is their straight-line displacement from the start?
options: 3 km
4 km
5 km
7 km
questions.rationale: This forms a 3-4-5 right triangle, so the straight-line displacement (the hypotenuse) is 5 km, even though the total path distance walked was 7 km.
